title: Kronecker's Jugendtraum (Hilbert's 12th)
description: Hilbert's 12th Problem asks to extend the Kronecker-Weber theorem: find explicit generators for all abelian extensions of number fields.

overview.historicalContext: Kronecker's Jugendtraum ('youthful dream') originated in 1853 when Leopold Kronecker expressed his vision that all abelian extensions of imaginary quadratic fields arise from the theory of elliptic functions with complex multiplication. Heinrich Weber proved the Kronecker-Weber theorem in 1886, establishing that all abelian extensions of the rationals are contained in cyclotomic fields. In 1896, David Hilbert included the generalization to arbitrary number fields as Problem 12 in his famous list of 23 problems. The 1920s saw Takagi, Artin, and Hasse develop abstract class field theory, which classifies abelian extensions but does not provide explicit generators. The theory of complex multiplication was made rigorous by Deuring and Shimura in the 1930s-1960s, solving the imaginary quadratic case. In the 1970s-1980s, Harold Stark formulated conjectures using L-function special values that would address real quadratic fields. The problem remains open for general number fields and connects deeply to the Langlands program.
overview.problemStatement: Given a number field K, find explicit analytic functions whose special values generate all abelian extensions of K. Solved for K = Q (cyclotomic fields) and K = imaginary quadratic (CM elliptic curves); open in general.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization proves that cyclotomic extensions of Q have abelian Galois groups (via the isomorphism Gal(Q(zeta_n)/Q) = (Z/nZ)^x and its commutativity), states the Kronecker-Weber theorem, defines the CM solution for imaginary quadratic fields, and discusses the open cases including Stark conjectures and the Langlands program.
keyInsights: For Q, the solution is purely algebraic: abelian extensions correspond exactly to cyclotomic fields generated by roots of unity
The Galois group Gal(Q(zeta_n)/Q) is isomorphic to (Z/nZ)^x, proven in Lean via IsCyclotomicExtension.autEquivPow
For imaginary quadratic fields, the solution uses complex analysis: j-invariants and torsion points on CM elliptic curves generate all abelian extensions
Class field theory classifies abelian extensions abstractly (via the Artin reciprocity map) but does not provide explicit generators - this gap is what Hilbert's 12th problem asks to fill

The problem is fundamentally about connecting algebraic number theory to complex analysis, a bridge that exists for Q (exponential function) and imaginary quadratic fields (elliptic functions) but not for general number fields

sections.title: Part I: Basic Definitions
sections.summary: Defines abelian extensions (Galois + commutative Galois group), the AbelianExtension type class, and cyclotomic extensions. These are the foundational objects for Hilbert's 12th problem.

sections.title: Part II: The Kronecker-Weber Theorem
sections.summary: States the Kronecker-Weber theorem (every finite abelian extension of Q is cyclotomic) and proves that cyclotomic extensions have abelian Galois groups via the isomorphism Gal(Q(zeta_n)/Q) = (Z/nZ)^x. Also proves the degree formula [Q(zeta_n):Q] = phi(n).

sections.title: Part III: Complex Multiplication
sections.summary: Defines imaginary and real quadratic fields, and states the CM solution for imaginary quadratic fields: j-invariants and torsion points on CM elliptic curves generate all abelian extensions.

sections.title: Part IV: Artin Reciprocity and Class Field Theory
sections.summary: Describes the Artin reciprocity law and class field theory, which abstractly classifies abelian extensions via the idele class group but does not provide explicit generators.

sections.title: Part V: What Remains Open
sections.summary: States Hilbert's 12th Problem in general and proves it is solved for Q (via Kronecker-Weber) and imaginary quadratic fields (via CM theory). The real quadratic and general cases remain open.

sections.title: Part VI: Known Partial Results and Examples
sections.summary: Provides concrete examples: Q(i) as CyclotomicField 4, Q(sqrt(-3)) as CyclotomicField 3, and proves irreducibility of cyclotomic polynomials over Z.

sections.title: Part VII: Stark Conjectures
sections.summary: Describes the Stark conjectures as a modern approach using L-function special values at s=0 to construct 'Stark units' generating abelian extensions, particularly for real quadratic fields.

sections.title: Part VIII: Summary
sections.summary: Summarizes the status of Hilbert's 12th Problem: solved for Q and imaginary quadratic fields, open for real quadratic and general fields. Connects to the Langlands program and modern arithmetic geometry.

conclusion.summary: Hilbert's 12th Problem is solved for Q (by the Kronecker-Weber theorem using cyclotomic fields) and for imaginary quadratic fields (by CM theory using j-invariants and elliptic curve torsion). The general case remains open and represents one of the deepest unsolved problems connecting number theory to complex analysis.
conclusion.implications: This problem initiated class field theory, one of the crowning achievements of 20th-century mathematics. The Kronecker-Weber theorem is the prototype for explicit class field theory. The CM solution for imaginary quadratic fields connects number theory to elliptic curves and modular forms, foreshadowing the Shimura-Taniyama conjecture (proved by Wiles). Modern approaches through the Langlands program and Stark conjectures continue to drive fundamental research in arithmetic geometry.
openQuestions: What are explicit generators for abelian extensions of real quadratic fields? The Stark conjectures predict answers via L-function values at s=0.
Can the Langlands program provide a conceptual framework for solving Hilbert's 12th problem in general?
What is the role of higher-dimensional CM theory (abelian varieties with many endomorphisms) in extending the solution beyond imaginary quadratic fields?
Are there explicit generators related to p-adic L-functions or Iwasawa theory for abelian extensions of general number fields?
